questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the device token issued by APNs?

options.text: It stores user payment card details for in-app purchases.
options.explanation: Payment credentials are encrypted in Secure Enclave, not device tokens.

options.explanation: Device tokens identify installed apps on specific physical devices.

questions.prompt: Why can an app not assume its APNs device token will remain constant forever?

options.explanation: Tokens are not fixed hardware IDs and change across system lifecycle events.

options.text: APNs rotates device tokens randomly every thirty seconds.
options.explanation: Tokens do not rotate every thirty seconds; they change across lifecycle events.

options.text: Tokens expire immediately when the device disconnects from Wi-Fi.
options.explanation: Tokens remain valid across normal cellular and Wi-Fi transitions.

options.text: Apple deletes tokens whenever an app enters background mode.
options.explanation: Tokens persist while the app is in the background.

questions.prompt: Explain the differences between local notifications and push notifications in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that local notifications are scheduled on device with time, calendar, or location triggers
Explains that push notifications originate from a backend server and route through APNs to the device

questions.modelAnswer: Local notifications are scheduled directly on the user device by your application code using triggers like time intervals, calendar dates, or geographical locations. They require no internet connection or external servers to fire. In contrast, push notifications originate from your backend server, which sends formatted JSON payloads to Apple Push Notification service (APNs) for delivery to target devices.

questions.prompt: Describe the registration steps required to configure an app for remote push notifications in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Mentions requesting user authorization and calling registerForRemoteNotifications
Mentions receiving the device token in the app delegate and uploading it to the backend server

questions.modelAnswer: First, the app requests user permission using UNUserNotificationCenter and calls registerForRemoteNotifications. Next, iOS contacts APNs to generate an opaque device token and passes it to the app delegate. Finally, the app converts this binary token into a hexadecimal string and uploads it to its backend server so the server can address future pushes.

questions.prompt: Explain how to display notification banners when your app is in the foreground in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains implementing userNotificationCenter(_:willPresent:withCompletionHandler:) and calling the handler with presentation options

questions.modelAnswer: By default, iOS suppresses visual banners when the app is active in the foreground. To display them, you must assign an object to the UNUserNotificationCenter delegate. Then implement userNotificationCenter(_:willPresent:withCompletionHandler:) and invoke the completion handler with presentation options like banner and sound.

questions.prompt: Explain what a Notification Service Extension does and how it is triggered in 2 to 5 sentences.
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Explains that it intercepts remote notifications to download media or decrypt payloads before display
Identifies that it is triggered by setting mutable-content to 1 in the aps payload

questions.modelAnswer: A Notification Service Extension is an app extension that intercepts remote notifications before they are presented to the user. It is triggered when the push payload includes mutable-content set to 1 in the aps dictionary. Within a thirty-second execution window, the extension can download rich media attachments or decrypt end-to-end encrypted message payloads.

questions.prompt: Explain the architectural trade-offs and limits of using silent push notifications in 2 to 5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that silent pushes wake the app in the background without user alerts using content-available: 1
Discusses system throttling based on battery, Low Power Mode, and user usage patterns

questions.modelAnswer: Silent push notifications wake an app in the background using the content-available key without showing banners. While useful for refreshing data quietly, iOS aggressively throttles silent pushes to conserve battery. Delivery fails if the device is in Low Power Mode or the user rarely opens the app. Therefore, do not rely on silent push for critical tasks.
